subject: Current Affairs
q: The SCO Heads of State summit held on 31 August–1 September 2025 took place in which Chinese city?
explanation: Leaders of the 10-member Shanghai Cooperation Organisation met in Tianjin, where President Xi Jinping called for a new SCO development bank.

subject: Current Affairs
q: At the September 2025 SCO summit in Tianjin, China proposed the creation of a new:
explanation: Xi Jinping called for a new SCO development bank and announced grants and loans for members, part of Beijing's push for alternatives to Western-led institutions.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The severe Punjab floods of late August–September 2025 were caused mainly by the swelling of which three rivers?
explanation: Flooding on the Ravi, Sutlej and Chenab affected about four million people in Pakistan, with some two million forced from their homes in Punjab.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), inaugurated in September 2025, is built on which river?
explanation: Ethiopia inaugurated GERD, Africa's largest hydroelectric dam, on the Blue Nile on 9 September 2025; downstream Egypt and Sudan fear for their water security.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Who became Nepal's first woman prime minister in September 2025, heading an interim government after the 'Gen Z' protests?
explanation: Former Chief Justice Sushila Karki was appointed interim prime minister on 12 September 2025 after deadly youth-led anti-corruption protests toppled the government.

subject: Current Affairs
q: An emergency Arab-Islamic summit was held in September 2025 in Doha in response to:
o: An Israeli strike on Hamas leaders in Qatar
An Iranian missile attack on Bahrain
A Houthi attack on Saudi oil facilities
The closure of the Suez Canal
explanation: Israel attacked Hamas leaders in Doha on 9 September 2025; Arab and Islamic leaders met in Qatar in solidarity, and the GCC pledged to activate its joint defence mechanism.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In September 2025, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed a Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement in which city?
explanation: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman signed the pact in Riyadh on 17 September 2025. It treats aggression against either country as aggression against both.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Under the Pakistan–Saudi Arabia Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement of September 2025, aggression against either country is to be treated as:
o: A matter for UN Security Council referral only
Grounds for consultation within the OIC
A trigger for economic sanctions only
explanation: The joint statement said any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both, a collective-defence clause similar in spirit to NATO's Article 5.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In September 2025, which group of countries formally recognised the State of Palestine on the same day, 21 September?
o: United States, Germany, Japan and Italy
United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and Portugal
India, Brazil, South Africa and Indonesia
explanation: The UK, Canada, Australia and Portugal announced recognition on 21 September 2025, ahead of the UN General Assembly high-level week; about 147 of 193 UN members then recognised Palestine.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In September 2025, which three military-ruled states announced their joint withdrawal from the International Criminal Court?
explanation: The three states of the Alliance of Sahel States, which had already left ECOWAS, said they were leaving the ICC to assert their 'sovereignty'.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In September 2025, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir held talks with President Donald Trump at:
explanation: The Oval Office meeting on 25 September 2025 was Shehbaz Sharif's first with Trump and the first joint appearance of Pakistan's civilian and military leaders before a US president in years.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In Moldova's parliamentary election of September 2025, which party won with about half of the vote?
explanation: The pro-EU PAS, associated with President Maia Sandu, won about 50 percent amid claims of Russian interference, keeping Moldova on its EU path.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In October 2025, the International Criminal Court delivered its first conviction for crimes committed in Darfur against:
o: Omar al-Bashir, former president of Sudan
Ali Kushayb, a former Janjaweed leader
explanation: Ali Muhammad Ali Abd-Al-Rahman ('Ali Kushayb') was found guilty of war crimes and crimes against humanity committed in Darfur in the 2000s.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Nobel Peace Prize 2025 was awarded to:
explanation: The Norwegian Nobel Committee honoured the Venezuelan opposition leader for her work promoting democratic rights and a peaceful transition to democracy in Venezuela.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The October 2025 international summit at which leaders signed a declaration backing the Gaza ceasefire was held in:
explanation: World leaders gathered in the Egyptian resort on 13 October 2025, led by President Trump and mediators Egypt, Qatar and Türkiye, to sign a declaration backing the ceasefire.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The 'Trump Declaration for Enduring Peace and Prosperity' on Gaza, signed in October 2025, was signed by the leaders of the United States and which three countries?
o: Saudi Arabia, Jordan and the UAE
explanation: Trump, Egypt's el-Sisi, Qatar's Emir Tamim and Türkiye's Erdogan signed the declaration as the mediating states; neither Israel nor Palestine was a party.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In October 2025, Pakistan was elected by the UN General Assembly to which body for the 2026–2028 term?
explanation: Pakistan won 178 votes for a three-year term on the 47-member Human Rights Council beginning 1 January 2026.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In October 2025, Colonel Michael Randrianirina was sworn in as president after a military takeover in which country?
explanation: The takeover followed mass protests over water and power shortages; President Andry Rajoelina fled into exile.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The immediate Pakistan–Afghanistan ceasefire agreed in Doha in October 2025 was mediated by:
explanation: After a week of deadly border clashes, the two defence ministers agreed a ceasefire in Doha on 19 October 2025 in talks mediated by Qatar and Türkiye; follow-up talks were held in Istanbul.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In October 2025, Pakistan launched its first hyperspectral satellite from which country?
explanation: SUPARCO's first hyperspectral satellite was launched from China and is meant to improve environmental monitoring, urban planning and disaster management.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Who became Japan's first woman prime minister in October 2025?
explanation: Japan's parliament confirmed LDP leader Sanae Takaichi as prime minister on 21 October 2025, replacing Shigeru Ishiba after a coalition deal with the Japan Innovation Party.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In its advisory opinion of October 2025, the International Court of Justice said Israel must facilitate aid to Gaza, including through which UN agency?
explanation: The ICJ said Israel, as occupying power, must allow aid into Gaza and support UN bodies, including the relief agency for Palestine refugees, UNRWA.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which country became the 11th member of ASEAN in October 2025?
explanation: Timor-Leste (East Timor) was admitted at the Kuala Lumpur summit on 26 October 2025, ASEAN's first new member in 26 years after it applied in 2011.

subject: Current Affairs
q: At the ASEAN summit in Kuala Lumpur in October 2025, President Trump co-signed a peace agreement between which two countries?
explanation: The deal, co-signed with Malaysia's Anwar Ibrahim, built on the ceasefire that halted deadly Thailand–Cambodia border fighting in July 2025.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In October 2025, Sudan's army withdrew from el-Fasher, its last stronghold in Darfur, leaving the city to:
explanation: Army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan admitted the retreat from the North Darfur capital; the UN warned of RSF atrocities against civilians.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Hurricane Melissa, the strongest storm on record to hit the island, made landfall as a Category 5 hurricane in October 2025 in:
explanation: Melissa struck Jamaica on 28 October 2025 with maximum sustained winds of about 295 km/h, well above the Category 5 threshold.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In the Dutch general election of October 2025, which party, led by Rob Jetten, nearly tripled its seats?
o: People's Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD)
explanation: The centre-left D66 surged while Geert Wilders' far-right PVV fell sharply from its record 2023 result.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In October 2025, Presidents Trump and Xi Jinping held their first face-to-face meeting since 2019 in which city?
explanation: The Busan meeting produced a trade truce: the US eased tariffs while China agreed to resume soybean imports and delay some rare-earth export controls.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Zohran Mamdani, elected in November 2025 as the first Muslim and South Asian mayor of New York City, defeated:
explanation: Mamdani won the mayoral race against former New York governor Andrew Cuomo, becoming the first Muslim to lead the largest US city.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Khaled El-Enany, elected Director-General of UNESCO in November 2025, is from which country?
explanation: The Egyptologist and former antiquities minister was elected at the General Conference in Samarkand with 172 of 174 votes, succeeding Audrey Azoulay; he is the first Director-General from an Arab country.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Paul Biya, described as the world's oldest ruler, was sworn in for an eighth term in November 2025 as president of:
explanation: The 92-year-old was sworn in after a disputed election that was followed by deadly protests.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In November 2025, Ahmed al-Sharaa became the first leader of which country to visit the White House since its independence in 1946?
explanation: Trump hosted the Syrian president and the US extended the suspension of Caesar Act sanctions for another 180 days.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In November 2025, a suicide bomber killed 12 people outside which building in Islamabad?
explanation: The blast near the crowded entrance of the Islamabad district court on 11 November 2025 was one of the deadliest attacks in the capital in years.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which new court was established in Pakistan by the 27th Constitutional Amendment of November 2025?
explanation: The 27th Amendment created a Federal Constitutional Court to hear constitutional matters, taking such cases away from the Supreme Court.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The 27th Constitutional Amendment (2025) created the new post of Chief of Defence Forces, to be held by:
o: The Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee
explanation: The amendment created the Chief of Defence Forces as head of the armed forces, a post held concurrently by the army chief.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Who took oath in November 2025 as the first Chief Justice of Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court?
explanation: President Asif Ali Zardari administered the oath to Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan on 14 November 2025, after the 27th Amendment created the court.

subject: Current Affairs
q: UN Security Council Resolution 2803 of November 2025 authorised the Board of Peace to establish a temporary:
o: UN peacekeeping mission in southern Lebanon
Naval mission in the Red Sea
Monitoring mission on the Golan Heights
explanation: Adopted 13–0 with China and Russia abstaining, Resolution 2803 endorsed the US-backed plan for Gaza and welcomed the Board of Peace as a transitional administration.

subject: Current Affairs
q: During Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's visit to Washington in November 2025, the United States designated Saudi Arabia as a:
o: Founding member of the Board of Peace
explanation: The designation came with approval of an F-35 fighter jet deal, elevating US–Saudi military cooperation.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Under the arrangement agreed in November 2025, COP31 in 2026 is to be hosted in which city?
explanation: Türkiye holds the COP31 presidency and hosts the summit in Antalya, while Australia leads pre-COP negotiations together with Pacific nations.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The G20 leaders' summit of November 2025, the first ever held in an African country, took place in:
explanation: South Africa hosted the summit in Johannesburg on 22–23 November 2025 despite a boycott by the United States.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The UN climate conference COP30 was held in November 2025 in:
explanation: COP30 met in the Amazonian city of Belém and closed on 23 November 2025 with a package of decisions termed the 'global mutirão'.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The main COP30 decision, named 'Global Mutirão', called on countries to triple which kind of climate finance by 2035?
explanation: 'Mutirão' means collective effort; the decision calls for adaptation finance to be tripled by 2035, while a fossil-fuel roadmap was pursued only outside the formal UN text.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Wang Fuk Court fire of November 2025, the deadliest fire in Hong Kong in more than 75 years, occurred in which district?
explanation: The blaze burned through seven residential towers of the estate in Tai Po, New Territories, killing at least 146 people.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In November 2025, a military coup deposed President Umaro Sissoco Embaló in:
explanation: The army installed its chief of staff, General Horta Inta-A, as transitional president.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Who was appointed Pakistan's first Chief of Defence Forces in December 2025?
o: Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Babar Sidhu
explanation: President Zardari approved the appointment for five years on 4 December 2025 under the post created by the 27th Amendment; Munir continues as army chief.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Cyclone Ditwah, which left more than 600 people dead in late 2025, devastated which country?
explanation: Floods and landslides after Cyclone Ditwah killed at least 618 people in Sri Lanka by early December 2025.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In December 2025, the IMF Executive Board completed which reviews of Pakistan's programmes, releasing about US$1.2 billion?
o: First review of the EFF and first review of the RSF
Third review of the EFF and second review of the RSF
Final review of the Stand-By Arrangement
Second review of the EFF and first review of the RSF
explanation: The Board's December 2025 decision released about $1.2 billion under the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (approved in 2024) and the Resilience and Sustainability Facility.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In December 2025, which country became the first to ban children under 16 from major social media platforms?
explanation: Australia's world-first law blocked under-16s from ten large platforms, including Facebook, TikTok and Instagram.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In December 2025, former ISI chief Lt Gen (retd) Faiz Hameed was sentenced to 14 years' rigorous imprisonment by:
explanation: The military court found him guilty of engaging in political activities, violating the Official Secrets Act and misusing authority and resources.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In December 2025, the United States authorised a package of about US$686 million for Pakistan relating to:
o: Upgrading and supporting its F-16 fighter jets
Purchase of new F-35 fighter jets
Construction of a nuclear power plant
explanation: Washington approved advanced technology and sustainment support for Pakistan's F-16 fleet, a sign of warmer US–Pakistan ties.

subject: Current Affairs
q: José Antonio Kast won the presidential run-off of December 2025 in which country?
explanation: Kast won about 58 percent against Communist Party candidate Jeannette Jara, part of a wave of right-wing victories in Latin America.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In December 2025, Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi were each sentenced to 17 years in prison in which case?
explanation: A special court convicted the couple of misrepresenting the value of state gifts, including jewellery, received while Khan was prime minister.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In December 2025, a 75 percent stake in Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) was sold to a consortium led by:
explanation: The Arif Habib-led consortium won the auction with a Rs135 billion bid after several rounds against a Lucky Cement-led group, ending decades of state bailouts of the airline.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In December 2025, Belgium joined the case brought at the International Court of Justice by which country against Israel under the Genocide Convention?
explanation: Belgium joined other states such as Brazil, Colombia, Ireland, Mexico, Spain and Türkiye in intervening in South Africa's case.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In December 2025, Nasry Asfura of the National Party was declared winner of the presidential election in:
explanation: Electoral authorities confirmed the narrow victory of the Trump-backed former mayor of Tegucigalpa.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Barham Salih, a former president of Iraq, took office on 1 January 2026 as head of which UN body?
o: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
explanation: Salih, who was himself a refugee as a young Kurdish exile from Iraq, now leads the UN agency responsible for more than 117 million forcibly displaced people.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In January 2026, a US military operation in Caracas seized which leader and flew him to New York to face charges?
explanation: US forces captured the Venezuelan president and his wife on 3 January 2026; he was indicted in New York on narcoterrorism and drug-trafficking charges.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Who was sworn in as Venezuela's president in January 2026 after Nicolás Maduro was seized by US forces?
explanation: Rodríguez, previously vice president, was formally sworn in on 5 January 2026.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In January 2026, the White House announced US withdrawal from dozens of bodies, including the UN's main climate treaty body:
explanation: The list included 31 UN entities such as the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, the UN Population Fund and the UN Democracy Fund.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The EU–Mercosur free trade agreement, signed in January 2026 after 25 years of negotiations, was signed in:
explanation: Ursula von der Leyen signed the pact in Paraguay's capital; it links the EU with Mercosur members Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.
